response.query: What power-analysis approaches and sample-size guidelines apply to hierarchical/Bayesian models linking mechanical properties to tool-class outcomes?
response.answer: For hierarchical/Bayesian models, power analysis typically involves determining sample sizes based on desired precision and effect size, using simulation techniques and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods. Guidelines often suggest starting with a pilot study to inform priors and then iteratively refining the model.

results.title: Hierarchical Bayesian Approach - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
results.content: # Hierarchical Bayesian Approach. The hierarchical Bayesian approach is defined as a method in Bayesian analysis that allows for the modeling of complex relationships among parameters through nested priors, enabling a richer statistical understanding of problems. It utilizes Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) techniques to handle more intricate models, facilitating the calculation of posterior probabilities based on dependencies among multiple parameters. Hierarchical Bayesian modeling is able to provide a representation of the uncertainty as posterior distributions that can be directly interpreted as “a 95% probability of a parameter being included between the fixed bounds of the interval” (Kruschke and Vanpaemel, 2015). Assumed to be a function of the estimated model parameters, the LRVs were also represented as distributions that include the uncertainties derived from our assumptions, shown in Fig. 1. An advantage of hierarchical Bayesian modeling is the capability to handle variability, which cannot be interpreted by explanatory variables and is attributable to the specific properties of individual matrices and disinfection methods.
